citation: Sten Ludvigsen, Ulrike Cress, Nancy Law, Carolyn P. Rosé, & Gerry Stahl. (2016). Collaboration scripts and scaffolding. International Journal of Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning, 11, 381–385. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-016-9247-1
title: Squibs: a short-format submission genre for ijCSCL
description: The editors announce Squibs, a new submission genre for ijCSCL modeled on the Computational Linguistics Journal tradition. Squibs may include "short articles reporting technical advancements, brief discussions of thought-provoking findings, cutting-edge algorithms, or new data or tools of interest to the journal readership," and may raise awareness of emerging trends, proposed practice changes, or theoretical and methodological debates. The shorter format is intended to facilitate quicker turnaround for timely discussions.
requirements: Squib submissions should generally not exceed 3000 words
target_learning_goals: timely reflection, discussion, and growth in the learning sciences field
examples: The editors report already receiving submissions in this category at the time of writing

article_title: Welcome to the future: ijCSCL volume 2
citation: Gerry Stahl & Friedrich Hesse. (2007). Welcome to the future: ijCSCL volume 2. Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-007-9010-8
title: Flash-theme special issues on Scripting in CSCL, Methods for Evaluating CSCL, and Graphical Support for CSCL
description: A set of special issues ijCSCL began publishing in its second volume on topics that "flashed" up in the field through spontaneous practitioner concern rather than editorial solicitation. Reviews on these themes are coordinated by Associate Editors—Barbara Wasson for scripting, Claire O'Malley for evaluation methods, and Daniel D. Suthers for graphical support—in a move to broaden editorial responsibilities as the journal becomes more established. The mechanism is intended to let the journal "give voice to the concerns of the field in a timely and flexible way."
requirements: Open responsiveness to workshop-originated topic proposals from practitioners, and Associate Editors to coordinate theme-based reviews.
constraints: The themes were not solicited by the ijCSCL Editorial Board but arose from practitioner workshops and concerns.
target_learning_goals: Advancing CSCL research on scripting, evaluation methods, and graphical support
examples: This year's volume begins with two papers on the flash theme of Learning in Communities, drawn from a 2006 Penn State workshop attended by 29 researchers and sponsored by the NSF.

citation: Monique Grandbastien, Rosemary Luckin, Riichiro Mizoguchi, Vincent Aleven. (2016). Preface to the IJAIED 25th Anniversary Issue. Int J Artif Intell Educ. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-015-0092-6
title: IJAIED 25th anniversary issue of 35 invited retrospective articles by authors of highly-cited papers
description: The 25th anniversary issue of IJAIED comprises invited short articles in which authors of the journal's most impactful original research papers reflect on their classic article, including subsequent developments and future directions. The editors write that they "approached the authors of highly-cited articles from the journal's history to write a new, short article that presented a new outlook on the line of work featured in their historic article". The 35 resulting articles went through the journal's regular peer review process.
requirements: Authors had to meet an objective highly-cited threshold of 100 citations as listed in Google Scholar
Each invited article had to address the seven questions posed by the editors
target_learners: researchers new to the field of artificial intelligence in education
target_learning_goals: understanding the intellectual history and state of the art of AI in education research
examples: 35 invited retrospective articles compiled for the journal's 25th year of operation, each reviewed under the journal's stringent peer review process

title: Special issue collection on Artificial Intelligence for Higher Education in the COVID-19 era (International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 2024)
description: This element is the special issue collection announced by the journal's editor's note, titled "Special Issue on Artificial Intelligence for Higher Education in the COVID-19 era: Emerging Technologies, Challenges, and Pedagogy-informed Applications". The note states the special issue "features 2 papers" which were "rigorously reviewed according to journal standards", and that the papers are available via the journal homepage's Collections link. The guest editors acknowledged are Professor Samira Hosseini (Tecnologico de Monterrey, Mexico), Professor Olga C. Santos (Computer Science School, UNED, Spain), Professor Gwanggil Jeon (Incheon National University, Korea), and Professor Rose Luckin (UCL Knowledge Lab, United Kingdom). The note itself contributes no findings; it serves as a pointer to the collection.
requirements: Access to the collection requires the journal homepage, since the note says the papers are available via the “Collections” link on the International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education homepage.
constraints: The editor's note itself contains no research content, findings, or learning-design claims; it only acknowledges the guest editors and announces the two-paper collection.
target_learning_goals: applications of artificial intelligence to higher education teaching and learning in the COVID-19 era
examples: The note lists the four guest editors and their institutions and states the special issue features two papers rigorously reviewed according to journal standards.
